html:
The army general who took power in Indonesia after a failed coup in 1965 and ruled as president until 1998, the longest in its history.

Born to a poor family near Yogyakarta, Suharto served in the Dutch colonial army, then in a Japanese-trained force, then in the army of the revolution. On 1 October 1965, after a group of officers killed six generals, he took control of the army and blamed the Communist Party. In the mass killings that followed, the army and allied militias killed at least half a million people. He eased Sukarno aside and became president in 1967.

His "New Order" brought decades of growth. Oil money, foreign investment and the Green Revolution cut poverty sharply. It also brought censorship, a tame parliament, the brutal invasion of East Timor in 1975, and corruption on a vast scale, much of it by his own family.

The 1997 Asian financial crisis wrecked the economy, and mass protests forced his resignation in May 1998. He was never tried.
sum: The army general who took power in Indonesia after a failed coup in 1965 and ruled as president until 1998, the longest in its history.
